rule: NES: 1 backdrop shared by both layers, 4 background palettes of 3 entries on 16x16 areas, 4 sprite palettes of 3 entries plus transparency on 8x8 tiles; every entry is a data/nes_palette.json entry number
notes: written by tools/art/make_ui_nes.py for the UI-NES card; the card that asked for the screens owns this file
backdrop $0F black is the shared backdrop of all three screens, and it is also the windows' bold outline
bg0 is the window in direction B: fill $02, rim $30, and the outline plus the right and bottom shadow in the shared backdrop $0F
bg1 is the accent, the name tab: fill $02, rim $28 gold, name in $30 white, outline in the backdrop
bg2 is the placeholder blocks: white rim, grey body, gold marker, ink outline
bg3 is spare and unused; the screens need 3 background palettes
sp0 covers the cursor and the enemy block (black $0F, gold $28, white $30)
sp1 covers the party block body (ink $0F, grey $00, white $30)

sp2 is the dialogue busts' gold row: ink $0F, gold $28, skin $36 carries all 36 tiles of spr_pp_portrait_prometheus.png. Card t_299de3bc and knowledge/PALETTE-RULINGS-2026-11-12.md section 3.1 re-solved it: the $02 interior came out of the three bust sheets, so a bust needs one row and the row it needs is its own two colours plus the ink. The party block's gold marker tile it used to name is on no shipped ui sheet: measured 2026-11-12, spr_pp_ui_party.png spends {00 0F 30} x6, {00 0F} x4 and {00} x2 and no gold at all, and the cursor is {28}, which sp0 carries

sp3 is the dialogue busts' white row: ink $0F, white $30, skin $36 carries all 36 tiles of spr_pp_portrait_guard.png and spr_pp_portrait_percy.png. It stops being spare on card t_299de3bc, and $02 leaves the sprite half with it: no shipped ui sprite sheet needs $02, the enemy is {0F 28 30} (sp0), the party {00 0F 30} (sp1) and the cursor {28} (sp0), and the two sheets that do need it, spr_pp_ui_window.png {02 0F 30} and spr_pp_ui_tab.png {02 0F 28}, are nine-slice background tiles pp_window_draw() draws from bg0 and bg1
